about.title: Norwalk Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself. In Norwalk, it might be a space heater in a Pioneer Boulevard apartment, a power tool bought off Rosecrans Avenue, a car seat that failed during one of the 413 injury collisions logged here in 2025, or a medication with a warning label that left out something important. When something you bought and used as intended hurts you, California law gives you a clear path. Under strict product liability, you generally don't have to prove the company was careless. You need to show the product had a defect — in how it was designed, how it was built, or how it warned you — and that the defect caused your injury. That shifts the weight of the case away from what the manufacturer knew and toward what the product actually did. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Norwalk residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles product cases on contingency. Keep the product, keep the packaging, and reach out when you're ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Norwalk Residents Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Works in Your Favor
items.desc: The attorneys in our network understand that a California product case usually turns on the defect and the harm it caused, not on proving the company was negligent. That distinction shapes how your claim is built from day one.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Be Examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Norwalk retailer that sold the item may each share responsibility. An independent attorney can identify who belongs in the claim rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Guidance Early
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of a defect case, and it's easy to lose or throw away in the stress after an injury. Connecting early means you get practical direction on keeping the item, its parts, receipts, and packaging intact.

items.question: A part in my car failed during a crash on Imperial Highway in Norwalk. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Norwalk recorded 546 people injured in traffic collisions in 2025, and some of those injuries are made worse by components that don't perform as designed, such as airbags, seatbelts, or tires. An attorney can look at the vehicle and the crash together and pursue the driver's insurer and the manufacturer where the facts support it. Don't let the car be scrapped or repaired before someone has inspected it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, which means you generally need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful is typically beside the point. That said, each case has its own facts, and an attorney can explain how the rule applies to yours.

items.question: I threw away the product after I got hurt. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: You may still have options, but preserving the product is strongly recommended because it is the central piece of evidence. If it's gone, gather whatever remains: photos, receipts, the box, the model number, medical records, and any similar item from the same batch. An attorney in the LawProactive network can review what you have and tell you honestly where things stand. There is no cost to ask.
